text: ORIGINAL AUDIO · 1949
*One couple.*
That means a *date*.
Not like just going around with the crowd.
Just me and the girl.
Well, that's all right.
Only... *what girl?*
Who?
The Strange Dating Rules\NAmerican Schools Taught in 1949
In *1949*, Coronet Instructional Films of Glenview,
\N\N\N\N\N\NAn AI-restored archival documentary demo
Illinois, shot this *color* film for American high school
Dating: Do's and Don'ts (1949)\NCoronet Instructional Films · Glenview, Illinois · Kodachrome print
*classrooms*. Its subject was not algebra or hygiene.
It was how to go on a *date*.
So what exactly were teenagers being *taught*,
and why were adults so *anxious* to teach it?
ORIGINAL AUDIO · 1949
*How do you choose a date?*
I. Choosing the girl
Whose company would you enjoy?
Well, one thing you can consider is *looks*.
What about Ann?
She knows how to have a good time, and how to make the fellow with her *relax*.
Have fun, too.
Yes, that's what a boy likes.
He wants to know he's *appreciated*.
Ann would be fun on a date.
Notice the *rule*. A girl is measured by how she makes a
boy feel: *appreciated*, *relaxed*, never *inferior*.
That was no accident.
The film's educational collaborator was *Reuben Hill*,
a family sociologist at the University of North
Carolina, and after the war Coronet produced *scores* of
Educational collaborator: Reuben Hill\NResearch Professor of Family Life, University of North Carolina
these social guidance films.
Historian Ken Smith calls them a postwar morality
offensive by educators, psychologists,
and the clergy.
ORIGINAL AUDIO · 1949
Ann? This is Woody.
II. Asking for a date
Well, I have a ticket for the Hi-Teen Carnival Saturday, and...
Well, would you like to go?
Why, yes, Woody.
I'll have to talk to *my folks* about it.
But I think I can go. That'll be fine.
Every wrong turn is a lesson in a *code*.
The boy *initiates*, offers a concrete plan,
names a time, and her parents hold a *veto*.
Historian Beth Bailey has shown how the prewar ideal of
*popularity*, measured by how many different people you
Median age at first marriage, 1950\Nwomen 20.3 · men 22.8   (U.S. Census Bureau, table MS-2)
dated, gave way after the war to pairing off and going
steady. The stakes were real.
In 1950 the median American bride was *twenty*,
the groom *twenty-two*, among the *youngest* the Census
Bureau has ever recorded.
Well, if you don't *overdo* on dating...
ORIGINAL AUDIO · 1949
III. The rules at home
Ed knows what I mean. *Weekends only*, and not too late.
I think the important thing about a date is to *have a good time*.
You don't need to spend a lot of money to do that.
You just enjoy whatever you do, whether it's movies or parties or anything.
And you leave your boyfriend *enough money*, so he'll ask you again.
Any girl who can't be *ready on time* for a date isn't good enough for my boy.
The *economics* are just as explicit.
He *pays*. She protects his *wallet*, so there will be a
second date. Her parents set the *curfew*,
and his mother sets the *schedule*.
"Teenager" enters common use in the 1940s\NSeventeen magazine founded 1944
The audience for all this was new.
The word *teenager* only entered everyday American speech
in the *1940s*, pushed by advertisers and by magazines
like *Seventeen*, founded in *1944*.
Adults were writing rules for a generation with spending
money of its own, and evenings far from the *front porch*.
ORIGINAL AUDIO · 1949
But *how do you say good night?*
IV. Saying good night
Perhaps...
Don't leave!
Well, it's getting late.
Yes, it is.
I'd ask you in for a bite to eat if it weren't so late.
Let's plan to get home in time for a *sandwich* or something next time.
Say, that sounds good.
I'll *call you* next week.
Will you?
Well, thanks so much.
I had a nice time.
So did I.
Good night, Woody.
Night, Ann.
So what does this film reveal about America in 1949?
A country just out of a war wanted *order*,
and it wanted it *early*: marriage in your early twenties,
after a courtship run by rules everyone could recite.
Median age at first marriage, 2024\Nwomen 28.6 · men 30.5   (NCFMR / American Community Survey)
The year before, Alfred *Kinsey*'s report on male sexual
behavior had become a *best seller* by documenting how far
real behavior strayed from the script.
Today the median American first marries at around *thirty*

for men and *twenty-eight* for women.
The film itself survives in the *public domain*,
because no renewal of its 1949 copyright has ever been
found. A reminder that the good night at the door was
never only about *manners*.
It was about who got to *decide*.
